acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a WBS skeleton generation call, when dispatched, then its schema no longer requires `estimate` (agentMinutes/tokens) per task

Given a per-task WBS detail generation call's response (already containing a real `estimate` in its template-filled field block, unchanged), when parsed via `wbs-assembler.js`'s `parseTaskDetailBlock`, then `estimate` (agentMinutes/tokens) is now read back from it, alongside the existing `groupingRationale`/verification commands
Given a feature generated end-to-end with UC-01 applied, when `c.estimates()` runs, then it reports the same shape/semantics of effort totals as before UC-01
Given `wb-skeleton-check.js`/`wb-graph-checks.js`'s existing structural checks, when run against a skeleton produced under UC-01's shrunk schema, then all pass exactly as they do today

Given a real implementation or review dispatch, when it completes (success, failure, or timeout), then a raw transcript/response evidence file is persisted for that specific dispatch attempt, readable independently of the run's own in-progress state

Given a task with one or more verification commands, all already passing before its first attempt, when `_runTaskToResolution` begins that attempt, then neither the implementation agent nor the review agent is ever dispatched, and the task is marked `'skipped'`

Given a task with one or more verification commands, at least one failing before its first attempt, when `_runTaskToResolution` begins that attempt, then a normal implementation dispatch proceeds, unchanged from today
Given a task with zero verification commands, when `_runTaskToResolution` begins its first attempt, then it is never short-circuited — a normal implementation dispatch proceeds
Given a task's second or later attempt, when `_runTaskToResolution` begins that attempt, then it is never short-circuited regardless of current verification state

Given a real run exercising UC-03's short-circuit on at least one task and a normal dispatch on at least one other, when measured, then the short-circuited task's wall-clock/token cost is near-zero compared to the normally-dispatched task
Given all changes are delivered, when `npm test` runs, then all tests pass: new regression tests for AC-01 through AC-10, and a full-suite regression
